features.Target: Your Pokémon with at least 1 Tutor Point.
features.Effect: The target loses 1 Tutor Point. Pick a Move in the target's Move List. The picked move is now permanently Psychic-Type, and may have different effects. See the Types Changes section (page 468) for more information and suggestions. A Pokémon may have only one Move-Sync'd Move in their Move List at a time; to Sync a new Move, the old Move must be forgotten.

features.Name: Psionic Sponge
features.Effect: Your Psychic-Type Pokémon may activate Psychic Sponge as a Shift Action to add a Psychic Type Move known by an ally within X meters to their Move List until the end of their turn. This does not allow them to have duplicate Moves in their Move List. This Feature may only be used once per Pokémon per Scene, and X is equal to your Type-Linked Skill Rank.

features.Name: Mindbreak
features.Prerequisites: [[feature:Psionic Sponge]], Adept Focus or Occult Education
features.Target: Your Psychic-Type Pokémon
features.Effect: While this Feature is Bound, the target's damaging Psychic-Type Moves gain a +1 Bonus to Effect Range and a +3 Bonus to Damage Rolls for each of the following conditions that the target is suffering: [[status:Bad Sleep]], [[status:Confusion]], [[move:Curse]], [[status:Disabled]], [[status:Flinch]], [[status:Infatuation]], [[status:Rage]], or Suppression.

features.Name: Psychic Resonance
features.Prerequisites: [[feature:Psionic Sponge]], Expert Focus or Occult Education
features.Trigger: Your Pokémon hits a foe with a Psychic-Type Status Move
features.Effect: Your Pokémon may use the Move [[move:Encore]] against the triggering foe, as if it was on their Move List.

features.Name: Force of Will
features.Prerequisites: [[feature:Psionic Sponge]], Master Focus or Occult Education
features.Trigger: Your Pokémon uses a Psychic-Type Status Move with a range of [[keyword:Blessing]], Field, [[keyword:Hazard]], or Self.
features.Effect: Your Pokémon may immediately use another Psychic-Type Status Move from its Move List with a range of [[keyword:Blessing]], Field, [[keyword:Hazard]], or Self.

features.Name: Type Ace
features.Prerequisites: 2 Different Rock-Type Pokémon, Novice Combat or Survival OR [[edge:Elemental Connection]] (Rock), 1 Rock-Type Pokémon, Novice Combat or Survival
features.Target: Your Pokémon with at least 2 Tutor Points remaining.
features.Effect: The target loses 2 Tutor Points and learns [[ability:Last Chance]] (Rock) or [[ability:Type Strategist]] (Rock). You may target a Pokémon only once with [[feature:Type Ace]].

features.Name: Type Refresh
features.Target: Your Pokémon
features.Effect: The target regains one use of a Rock-Type Scene-Frequency Move, and refreshes the Frequency of all Rock-Type EOT-Frequency Moves. A Target can be affected by [[feature:Type Refresh]] only once per Scene.

features.Name: Move Sync
features.Target: Your Pokémon with at least 1 Tutor Point.
features.Effect: The target loses 1 Tutor Point. Pick a Move in the target's Move List. The picked move is now permanently Rock-Type, and may have different effects. See the Types Changes section (page 468) for more information and suggestions. A Pokémon may have only one Move-Sync'd Move in their Move List at a time; to Sync a new Move, the old Move must be forgotten.

features.Name: Gravel Before Me
features.Trigger: Your Rock-Type Pokémon misses all targets with a Rock-Type attack, receives an Injury, suffers a Critical Hit, or Faints.
features.Effect: Create a [[move:Stealth Rock]] [[keyword:Hazard]] adjacent to your Pokémon.

features.Name: Bigger and Boulder
features.Prerequisites: [[feature:Gravel Before Me]], Adept Combat or Survival
features.Trigger: Your Pokémon hits with a damaging Rock-Type Move
features.Effect: All targets hit by the triggering Move are pushed a number of meters equal to half your Type-Linked Skill Rank or less, and they become [[status:Vulnerable]] for one full round. Create a [[move:Stealth Rock]] [[keyword:Hazard]] adjacent to each foe hit this way.

features.Name: Tough as Schist
features.Prerequisites: [[feature:Gravel Before Me]], Expert Combat or Survival
features.Target: Your Rock-Type Pokémon
features.Effect: While this Feature is Bound, allied [[move:Stealth Rock]] Hazards within 4 meters of your Pokémon are not used when a foe triggers them unless you want them to be. Whenever the target takes Super-Effective Damage from a Water, Grass, Ground, Fighting, or Steel Type Attack, they may consume an allied [[move:Stealth Rock]] [[keyword:Hazard]] within 4 meters to create temporary armor that grants them Damage Reduction equal to your Type-Linked Skill Rank for one full round.

features.Name: Gneiss Aim
features.Prerequisites: [[feature:Gravel Before Me]], Master Combat or Survival
features.Trigger: Your Pokémon misses with a Damaging Rock-Type Move
features.Effect: The Move gains the [[keyword:Smite]] keyword for that use.

features.Name: Type Ace
features.Prerequisites: 2 Different Steel-Type Pokémon, Novice Athletics or Intimidate OR [[edge:Elemental Connection]] (Steel), 1 Steel-Type Pokémon, Novice Athletics or Intimidate
features.Target: Your Pokémon with at least 2 Tutor Points remaining.
features.Effect: The target loses 2 Tutor Points and learns [[ability:Last Chance]] (Steel) or [[ability:Type Strategist]] (Steel). You may target a Pokémon only once with [[feature:Type Ace]].

features.Name: Type Refresh
features.Target: Your Pokémon
features.Effect: The target regains one use of a Steel-Type Scene-Frequency Move, and refreshes the Frequency of all Steel-Type EOT-Frequency Moves. A Target can be affected by [[feature:Type Refresh]] only once per Scene.

features.Name: Move Sync
features.Target: Your Pokémon with at least 1 Tutor Point.
features.Effect: The target loses 1 Tutor Point. Pick a Move in the target's Move List. The picked move is now permanently Steel-Type, and may have different effects. See the Types Changes section (page 468) for more information and suggestions. A Pokémon may have only one Move-Sync'd Move in their Move List at a time; to Sync a new Move, the old Move must be forgotten.

features.Name: Polished Shine
features.Effect: The Effect Range of your Pokémon's Steel-Type Moves is increased by +2.

features.Name: Iron Grit
features.Target: Your Pokémon
features.Effect: When this Feature becomes Bound, the target gains +1 Defense Combat Stage. While the Feature remains bound, the target's Defense Stat cannot be lowered, and its Defense Combat Stages cannot be lowered.

features.Name: Assault Armor
features.Trigger: Your Pokémon hits with a Steel-Type attack
features.Effect: Your Pokémon may add its Defense Stat to their Damage Roll in place of the attack's normal offensive stat.

features.Name: True Steel
features.Trigger: Your Steel-Type Pokémon is hit by a damaging attack
features.Effect: Your Pokémon gains Damage Reduction against the attack equal to your Type-Linked Skill Rank. Additionally, calculate Type Effectiveness with this attack as if your Pokémon has no Typings besides Steel.

features.Name: Type Ace
features.Prerequisites: 2 Different Water-Type Pokémon, Novice Athletics or Intuition OR [[edge:Elemental Connection]] (Water), 1 Water-Type Pokémon, Novice Athletics or Intuition
features.Target: Your Pokémon with at least 2 Tutor Points remaining.
features.Effect: The target loses 2 Tutor Points and learns [[ability:Last Chance]] (Water) or [[ability:Type Strategist]] (Water). You may target a Pokémon only once with [[feature:Type Ace]].

features.Name: Type Refresh
features.Target: Your Pokémon
features.Effect: The target regains one use of a Water-Type Scene-Frequency Move, and refreshes the Frequency of all Water-Type EOT-Frequency Moves. A Target can be affected by [[feature:Type Refresh]] only once per Scene.

features.Name: Move Sync
features.Target: Your Pokémon with at least 1 Tutor Point.
features.Effect: The target loses 1 Tutor Point. Pick a Move in the target's Move List. The picked move is now permanently Water-Type, and may have different effects. See the Types Changes section (page 468) for more information and suggestions. A Pokémon may have only one Move-Sync'd Move in their Move List at a time; to Sync a new Move, the old Move must be forgotten.

features.Name: Flood!
features.Effect: Your Water-Type Pokemon may activate [[feature:Flood!]] as a Shift Action to use a damaging Water-Type Move as if had a range of Line 4 or Close Blast 2 instead of its usual range.

features.Name: Fishbowl Technique
features.Target: Your Pokémon
features.Effect: While this Stratagem is bound, your Pokémon may activate Moves and Abilities as if they were in Rainy Weather.

features.Name: Fountain of Life
features.Trigger: Your Water-Type Pokémon hits with a damaging Water-Type attack
features.Effect: You may choose to take a penalty to the Damage Roll for the attack up to triple your Type-Linked Skill Rank or up to half the rolled damage for the triggering attack, whichever is lower. Your Pokémon gains twice that value in Temporary Hit Points and may cure themselves of one Status Affliction. [[feature:Fountain of Life]] may only be used once per Scene per Pokémon.

features.Name: Aqua Vortex
features.Trigger: Your Pokémon hits with a damaging Water-Type attack
features.Effect: All targets of the attack are put in a [[keyword:Vortex]], and take a penalty to all Damage Rolls equal to your Type-Linked Skill Rank while in the [[keyword:Vortex]].

features.Name: Chef
features.Effect: You may use any Chef Recipe for which you qualify.

features.Name: Hits the Spot
features.Trigger: You or your Pokémon trade in a Digestion Buff
features.Effect: The target gains Temporary Hit Points equal to your Intuition Rank doubled. These Temporary Hit Points stack from any Temporary Hit Points granted by [[feature:Accentuated Taste]], the Digestion Buff or by the [[ability:Lunchbox]] Ability.

features.Name: Culinary Appreciation
features.Target: Your Pokémon with at least 2 Tutor Points remaining
features.Effect: The target loses 2 Tutor Points and gains the [[ability:Gluttony]] Ability.

features.Name: Accentuated Taste
features.Effect:
Whenever you create a Snack with a [[feature:Chef]] Feature, you may assign it a Taste chosen from Salty, Sour, Spicy, Dry, and Sweet. [[feature:Tasty Snacks]] must be assigned their corresponding Taste. Whenever a Pokémon trades in a Digestion Buff from a Snack with an assigned Taste they do not dislike, they gain the following bonuses:
» Salty: The user gains 5 Temporary Hit Points. This stacks with any Temporary Hit Points gained through [[feature:Chef]] Features, the [[ability:Lunchbox]] Ability, and the Digestion Buff.
» Spicy: Increase the user's Critical Hit Range by 1.
» Sour: Increase the user's Evasion against damaging attacks by 1.
» Dry: Increase the user's Effect Range of all attacks by 1.
» Bitter: The user gets a +1 Bonus to all Save Checks.
» Sweet: Increase the user's Initiative by 5.

features.Name: Complex Aftertaste
features.Target: You or an ally trades in a Digestion Buff from an item with a Taste
features.Effect: The target gains a Digestion Buff according to the Taste of the Snack granting the Buff. This Digestion Buff matches that of the corresponding basic Tasty Snack recipe.

features.Name: Dietician
features.Effect: Your Pokemon can benefit from a maximum of 7 [[feature:Vitamins]].

features.Name: Dumplings
features.Effect: You mix the two ingredients into one Snack that has the same effect as its ingredients. The two ingredients must be different items.

recipes.Name: Tasty Snacks
recipes.Effect: You create a [[feature:Salty Surprise]], [[feature:Spicy Wrap]], [[feature:Sour Candy]], [[feature:Dry Wafer]], [[feature:Bitter Treat]], or [[feature:Sweet Confection]].

recipes.Name: Salty Surprise
recipes.Effect: The user may trade in this Snack's Digestion Buff when being hit by an attack to gain 5 Temporary Hit Points. If the user likes Salty Flavors, they gain 10 Temporary Hit Points Instead. If the user dislikes Salty Food, they become Enraged.

recipes.Name: Spicy Wrap
recipes.Effect: The user may trade in this Snack's Digestion Buff when making a Physical attack to deal +5 additional Damage. If the user prefers Spicy Food, it deals +10 additional Damage instead. If the user dislikes Spicy Food, they become Enraged.

recipes.Name: Sour Candy
recipes.Effect: The user may trade in this Snack's Digestion Buff when being hit by a Physical Attack to increase their Damage Reduction by +5 against that attack. If the user prefers Sour Food, they gain +10 Damage Reduction instead. If the user dislikes Sour Food, they become Enraged.

recipes.Name: Dry Wafer
recipes.Effect: The user may trade in this Snack's Digestion Buff when making a Special attack to deal +5 additional Damage. If the user prefers Dry Food, it deals +10 additional Damage instead. If the user dislikes Dry Food, they become Enraged.

recipes.Name: Bitter Treat
recipes.Effect: The user may trade in this Snack's Digestion Buff when being hit by a Special Attack to increase their Damage Reduction by +5 against that attack. If the user prefers Bitter Food, they gain +10 Damage Reduction instead. If the user dislikes Bitter Food, they become Enraged.

recipes.Name: Sweet Confection
recipes.Effect: The user may trade in this Snack's Digestion Buff to gain +4 Evasion until the end of their next turn. If the user prefers Sweet Food, they gain +4 Accuracy as well. If the user dislikes Sweet Food, they become Enraged.

recipes.Name: Meal Planner
recipes.Effect: You may create the following items, based on your Intuition Rank.

recipes.Name: Hearty Meal
recipes.Ingredients: x2 Tiny Mushrooms; or x1 [[item:Big Mushroom]]; or x1 [[item:Balm Mushroom]], or x2 Power Herbs, White Herbs, or Mental Herbs
recipes.Effect: You create up to five Hearty Meals, which may be consumed by Trainers as an Extended Action. When consumed, that Trainer gains +2 to their Max AP until the end of their next extended rest. A Trainer may only be under the effect of one [[feature:Hearty Meal]] at a time. Hearty Meals not consumed within 20 minutes of being created lose all flavor and all effect.

recipes.Name: Bait Mixer
recipes.Effect: You may create [[item:Bait]]. For ₽50 more, you may create [[item:Bait]] as Super Bait or Vile Bait instead. Super Bait works like regular [[item:Bait]], but you may add your Intuition Rank to 1d20 Rolls made to attract Pokémon. Vile Bait works like regular [[item:Bait]], but Pokémon that eat it are [[status:Poisoned]].

recipes.Name: Preserves
recipes.Effect: The user creates x2 Units of [[feature:Preserves]] from the [[keyword:Berry]], Herb, or Mushroom. [[feature:Preserves]] have the same effect as the consumable from which they were made.

recipes.Name: Leftovers
recipes.Effect: You create [[item:Leftovers]].

recipes.Name: Vitamins
recipes.Effect: You create an [[item:HP Up]], [[item:Protein]], [[item:Iron]], [[item:Calcium]], [[item:Zinc]], or [[item:Carbos]] for ₽2450, or [[item:Stat Suppressants]] for ₽200.

features.Name: Chronicler
features.Target: A Pokémon, Trainer, Move, or Location.
features.Effect: You make Record of the target. Records can be placed in an Archive as an Extended Action. When you take [[feature:Chronicler]], you gain one Archive.
features.Archives:
» Profile Archive: You may place Records of Pokémon and Trainers in your Profile Archive. You gain a +2 bonus to Charm, Guile, Command, Intimidate, and Intuition Checks targeting Pokémon and Trainers in your Profile Archive.
» Technique Archive: You may place Records of Moves in your Technique Archive. You and your Pokémon gain +2 Evasion against Moves in your Technique Archives.
» Travel Archive: You may place Records of Locations in your Travel Archive. When you gain Travel Archive, choose [[ability:Keen Eye]] or Perception. While you are in a Location in your Travel Archive, you have the Chosen Ability and gain a +2 bonus to Perception Checks to notice the environment.

features.Name: Archival Training
features.Effect: Each Rank, you gain an Archive.

features.Name: Archive Tutor
features.Target: A Pokémon with 2 Tutor Points.
features.Effect: Select a Record in your Technique Archive that is of a Move that the target can learn by Level Up, TM or by Move Tutor. The target learns the Move and loses 2 Tutor Points. You can target someone else's Pokémon only once with [[feature:Archive Tutor]]; you may target your own Pokémon any number of times with [[feature:Archive Tutor]], but they must still abide by any Move Pool Limitations (ie: no more than 3 of the user's Move Pool can come from TMs or Tutor Moves).

features.Name: Targeted Profiling
features.Target: Your Pokémon
features.Effect: On the target's next turn, they act as if they had the [[ability:Mold Breaker]] Ability against all Pokémon and Trainers in your Profile Archive and gains a +2 bonus to Accuracy Rolls against these targets.

features.Name: Observation Party
features.Effect: While they are in a Location in your Travel Archive, your Pokémon have the Ability you chose when gaining Travel Archive and gain a +2 bonus to Perception Checks to notice the environment.

features.Name: Cinematic Analysis
features.Effect: You analyze a Record in one of your Archives. [[feature:Cinematic Analysis]]'s effect depends on the Archive the Record is in. Each of these effects may only be used once per Scene.
features.Character Study — Profile Archive: You may trigger Character Study when you or an ally makes a Charm, Command, Guile, Intimidate, or Intuition Check targeting the subject of your Record. Make a Perception Check and substitute the triggering Skill Check with the result.
features.Recreation — Technique Archive: Recreation may be triggered as your Pokémon gains Initiative. Select a Record of a Move in your Technique Archive that your Pokémon can learn by Level Up, TM, or Move Tutor. Your Pokémon may perform that Move as if it was on its Move List. You may select a specific Move only once per day.
features.Situational Awareness — Travel Archive: You may only use Situational Awareness if you analyze a Record of your current Location. When used this way, you may activate it as an [[keyword:Interrupt]]. Choose an ally; that ally may take their next action as [[keyword:Priority]] (Advanced).

features.Name: Fashionista
features.Prerequisites: Two of Charm, Command, Guile, Intimidate, or Intuition at Novice
features.Effect: You may craft any Fashionista Recipe for which you qualify.

features.Name: Dashing Makeover
features.Target: A Trainer or Pokémon
features.Effect: When you activate [[feature:Dashing Makeover]], choose one Equipment or Held Item you can create. While this Feature is Bound, the target gains the effects of the chosen item, as long as they would normally be able to equip it (ex: Trainers cannot equip Incense Items).They do not need to take up an Equipment or Held Item slot to gain this benefit. A target may only be affected by one instance of [[feature:Dashing Makeover]] at a time.

features.Name: Style is Eternal
features.Trigger: Your Pokémon is Disarmed or would have their Held Item removed by another effect such as [[move:Thief]] or [[move:Covet]]
features.Effect: Your Pokémon instead retains their Held Item. [[feature:Style is Eternal]] may only be used once per Scene per Pokémon.

features.Name: Accessorize
features.Prerequisites: [[feature:Dashing Makeover]], one Fashionista Skill at Adept
features.Effect: You may wear and benefit from two Accessory Slot Items at once. The two items must be of different types and must not share an effect. For example, a Fire Brace cannot be paired with another Fire Brace or a Fire Plate, but it could be paired with an Ice Brace, a Fire Booster, or a Stat Booster.

features.Name: Parfumier
features.Effect: Whenever you create an Incense Held Item, choose [[move:Sweet Scent]] or [[move:Aromatic Mist]]. While your Pokémon is holding that Incense Item in an active Held Item slot, they add the chosen Move to their Move List.

features.Name: Versatile Wardrobe
features.Target: Your Pokémon with at least 2 Tutor Points remaining
features.Effect: The target loses 2 Tutor Points and then becomes chic. Chic Pokémon gain two extra Held Item slots with which they can carry Held Items. However, the items in these slots have no effect and are not treated as equipped. As a Swift Action on their turn, Chic Pokémon may swap a currently active Held Item with an item stored in these slots. Chic Pokémon may not carry multiple items of the same type or with repeated effects.
features.Note: A Chic Pokémon does not become [[status:Suppressed]] until they switch a [[item:Choice Item]] into their active Held Item slot, but even if they then switch the [[item:Choice Item]] out, they remain [[status:Suppressed]] for the remainder of combat. A Mega-Evolved Chic Pokémon remains Mega-Evolved even if they switch their active Held Item.

features.Name: Dress to Impress
features.Prerequisites: [[feature:Versatile Wardrobe]], two Fashionista Skills at Expert
features.Target: Your Chic Pokémon
features.Effect: Your Pokémon gains the effect of all items in extra slots granted by [[feature:Versatile Wardrobe]] for one full round. [[feature:Dress to Impress]] may only target a Pokémon once per Scene.

recipes.Name: Contest Trends
recipes.Effect: You can create Contest Accessories for ₽750, [[item:Contest Fashion]] Items for ₽500, and [[item:Fancy Clothes]] for ₽2500.

recipes.Name: Basic Fashion
recipes.Effect: You create one of the [[feature:Basic Fashion]] Items below for which you have the chosen Fashionista Skill. These are Accessory Slot Items and may be used as Held Items by Pokémon.

recipes.Name: Adorable Fashion
recipes.Effect: The holder may activate this item once a Scene as a Free Action to gain +2 Evasion for one full round.

recipes.Name: Elegant Fashion
recipes.Effect: The holder may activate this item once a Scene as a Free Action when losing Combat Stages from a foe's effect to instead not lose those Combat Stages.

recipes.Name: Rad Fashion
recipes.Effect: The holder may activate this item once a Scene as a Free Action to gain a +4 bonus to a single Save Check.

recipes.Name: Rough Fashion
recipes.Effect: The holder may activate this item once a Scene as a Free Action to cause a foe within 5 meters to take a -2 penalty to all rolls for one full round.

recipes.Name: Slick Fashion
recipes.Effect: The holder may activate this item once a Scene as a Free Action when provoking an Attack of Opportunity to instead not provoke one.

recipes.Name: Practical Fashion
recipes.Effect: You can create [[item:Go-Goggles]], [[item:Safety Goggles]], or Winter Cloaks for ₽750.

recipes.Name: Focused Fashion
recipes.Effect: You can create Focus Bands and Focus Sashes for ₽2000.

recipes.Name: Incense Maker
recipes.Effect: You can create [[item:Lax Incense]] for ₽1000, [[item:Luck Incense]] for ₽900, and [[item:Full Incense]] for ₽450.

features.Name: Researcher
features.Prerequisites: An Education Skill at Novice Rank
features.Effect: Choose two Researcher Fields of Study. You may take Features from those Fields with this instance of [[feature:Researcher]]. Gain one Feature from a chosen Researcher Field for which you qualify.

features.Name: Breadth of Knowledge
features.Prerequisites: General Research Field, Novice General Education
features.Effect: You gain three Skill Edges for which you qualify. These Edges must be used to gain a Skill Edge with an Education Skill, or to gain an Edge that has an Education Skill as a Prerequisite that you meet.

features.Name: Bookworm
features.Effect: You gain X Study Points, where X is equal to 2 plus one more for every other General Research Feature you have. You may Drain Study Points to benefit from studying Books, instead of Draining your Action Points. Study Points are restored to your maximum after an Extended Rest, just like Action Points.

features.Name: Well Read
features.Effect: You may use your General Education Rank to qualify for Books, instead of the Book's usual Skill Prerequisites, provided you have the normal Prerequisite at at least Novice Rank.

features.Name: Echoes of the Future
features.Trigger: You or your Pokémon make a roll
features.Effect: You may roll twice and keep the best result.

features.Name: Breadth of Knowledge
features.Prerequisites: General Research Field, Novice General Education
features.Effect: You gain three Skill Edges for which you qualify. These Edges must be used to gain a Skill Edge with an Education Skill, or to gain an Edge that has an Education Skill as a Prerequisite that you meet.

features.Name: Live and Learn
features.Trigger: You or your Pokémon miss with an attack, fail a Skill Check, or fail a Save Check
features.Effect: Add half of your General Education Rank to the next roll of the same type that the triggering user makes.

features.Name: Instant Analysis
features.Target: Your Pokémon with at least 2 Tutor Points remaining
features.Effect: Your Pokémon loses 2 Tutor Points and gains the [[ability:Forewarn]] Ability.

features.Name: Echoes of the Future
features.Trigger: You or your Pokémon make a roll
features.Effect: You may roll twice and keep the best result.

features.Name: Apothecary
features.Effect: You gain use any Apothecary Recipe for which you qualify.

features.Name: Patch Cure
features.Target: A Restorative Item
features.Effect: You distill the target, gaining 3 Restorative Patches. Restorative Patches have the same effect as the items from which they were created, but can only be applied as an Extended Action.

features.Name: Affliction Techniques
features.Trigger: You use a [[item:Antidote]], [[item:Burn Heal]], [[item:Ice Heal]], or [[item:Paralyze Heal]]
features.Effect:
If the target successfully cures the target of its linked Status Affliction, the item has additional effects.
» [[item:Antidote]]: The target gains +1 Special Defense Combat Stage.
» [[item:Burn Heal]] The target gains +1 Defense Combat Stage.
» [[item:Ice Heal]]: The target gains +1 Attack or Special Attack Combat Stage
» [[item:Paralyze Heal]]:The target gains +1 Speed Combat Stage.

features.Name: Medicinal Blend
features.Trigger: You or your Pokémon make a roll
features.Effect:
Ingredients: Two Restoratives, or a Restorative and an X-Item
Effect: You fuse the two Ingredients, creating an Item that has the properties of both. If you choose two Restoratives, they cannot be Restoratives with the same effect (you could not for example, mix a [[item:Potion]] and a [[item:Super Potion]]). If a Restorative Patch is used as an Ingredient, the resulting item can only be used as an Extended Action.

recipes.Name: Restorative Science
recipes.Effect: You create an [[item:Antidote]], [[item:Paralyze Heal]], Awakening, [[item:Burn Heal]], [[item:Ice Heal]], or [[item:Potion]].

recipes.Name: Super Cures
recipes.Effect: You can create Revives and Super Potions.

recipes.Name: Hyper Cures
recipes.Effect: You can create Full Heals for ₽300, Hyper Potions for ₽400, and Full Restores for ₽700.

recipes.Name: Performance Enhancers
recipes.Effect: You create a [[item:PP Up]] or [[item:Heart Booster]]. If you have a [[item:Heart Scale]], you may destroy the [[item:Heart Scale]] to create a [[item:Heart Booster]] without paying the monetary cost.

features.Name: Apothecary
features.Effect: You gain use any Apothecary Recipe for which you qualify.

features.Name: Patch Cure
features.Target: A Restorative Item
features.Effect: You distill the target, gaining 3 Restorative Patches. Restorative Patches have the same effect as the items from which they were created, but can only be applied as an Extended Action.

features.Name: Medical Techniques
features.Trigger: You apply a Restorative Item
features.Effect: The target gains a Tick of Hit Points, plus an additional amount of Hit Points equal to your Medicine Education Rank.

features.Name: Medicinal Blend
features.Trigger: You or your Pokémon make a roll
features.Effect:
Ingredients: Two Restoratives, or a Restorative and an X-Item
Effect: You fuse the two Ingredients, creating an Item that has the properties of both. If you choose two Restoratives, they cannot be Restoratives with the same effect (you could not for example, mix a [[item:Potion]] and a [[item:Super Potion]]). If a Restorative Patch is used as an Ingredient, the resulting item can only be used as an Extended Action.

recipes.Name: Restorative Science
recipes.Effect: You create an [[item:Antidote]], [[item:Paralyze Heal]], Awakening, [[item:Burn Heal]], [[item:Ice Heal]], or [[item:Potion]].

recipes.Name: Super Cures
recipes.Effect: You can create Revives and Super Potions.

recipes.Name: Hyper Cures
recipes.Effect: You can create Full Heals for ₽300, Hyper Potions for ₽400, and Full Restores for ₽700.

recipes.Name: Performance Enhancers
recipes.Effect: You create a [[item:PP Up]] or [[item:Heart Booster]]. If you have a [[item:Heart Scale]], you may destroy the [[item:Heart Scale]] to create a [[item:Heart Booster]] without paying the monetary cost.

features.Name: Crystal Artificer
features.Effect: You may use any [[feature:Crystal Artificer]] Recipe for which you qualify.

features.Name: Crystal Resonance
features.Effect: You roll an additional 3d6 when determining how many [[item:Shards]] you find when Dowsing.

features.Name: Rainbow Light
features.Trigger: You are wearing a [[feature:Rainbow Gem]]
features.Effect: You create a Rainbow lasting one full round. While this Rainbow persists, the Effect Range of all Allies is increased by +3.

features.Name: Fistful of Force
features.Trigger: You must have a Shard in your Main Hand or Off-Hand to use [[feature:Fistful of Force]].
features.Effect: You may destroy the Shard to use the Move [[move:Judgment]]. [[move:Judgment]]'s Type must be one of the Types associated with the used Shard. Instead of adding your Special Attack when using this attack, you may choose to add your Occult Education Rank tripled.

recipes.Name: Type Booster
recipes.Effects: You create a [[feature:Type Booster]]. The Type chosen must be one of the Types associated with the color of the shards used.

recipes.Name: Type Brace
recipes.Effects: You create a [[item:Type Brace]]. The Type chosen must be one of the Types associated with the color of the shards used.

recipes.Name: Focus Gem
recipes.Effect: You create a [[item:Focus]] that may crafted to be worn as your choice of an Accessory Item, Head Slot Item, or Hand or Off-Hand Item.

recipes.Name: Chakra Crystal
recipes.Effect: You create a Stat Booster.

recipes.Name: Rainbow Gem
recipes.Effect: You create a [[feature:Rainbow Gem]] that may crafted to be worn as your choice of an Accessory Item, Head Slot Item, or Hand or Off-Hand Item. This item has the same effect as a [[item:Focus]], except that as an Extended Action, any Trainer with Expert Occult Education Rank or higher may change which Stat the Rainbow Amulet is attuned to.

recipes.Name: Plate Crafter
recipes.Ingredients: A [[feature:Type Booster]] and a [[item:Type Brace]] of the same Type.
recipes.Effects: You create a [[item:Type Plate]] matching the [[feature:Type Booster]] and Brace used.

features.Name: Seed Bag
features.Rank 1 Prerequisites: [[edge:Green Thumb]], Adept General Education, Adept Survival
features.Target: A Willing Pokémon
features.Rank 1 Effect: You become adept at harvesting Seeds and Spores from Pokémon. You may target a willing Grass-Type Pokémon that knows [[move:Sleep Powder]], [[move:Stun Spore]], or [[move:Poison Powder]]. Add this move to your Move list for the remainder of the day. You may not use [[feature:Seed Bag]] to have multiple instances of the same move in your Move list. [[feature:Seed Bag]] may be used twice per day per Rank.
features.Rank 2 Effect: You may also harvest [[move:Cotton Spore]], [[move:Leech Seed]], [[move:Spore]], or [[move:Worry Seed]].

features.Name: Top Tier Berries
features.Effect:
You may grow additional Berries and Herbs, depending on the higher of your General Education or Survival Rank.
» Novice: You may grow Tier 2 Berries
» Adept: You may grow Mental Herbs, Power Herbs, White Herbs, and Tiny Mushrooms.
» Expert: You may grow Revival Herbs, Energy Roots,Big Mushrooms, and Tier 3 Berries
» Master: Increase the Soil Quality of all your plants by +1.

features.Name: Herb Lore
features.Effect:
You may create [[item:Energy Powder]], [[item:Heal Powder]], or [[item:Poultices]] from ingredients, as listed below.
[[item:Energy Powder]]: A [[item:Sitrus Berry]] or [[item:Tiny Mushroom]] creates x2 Energy Powders. An [[item:Energy Root]] creates x3 Energy Powders.
[[item:Heal Powder]]: A [[item:Lum Berry]] or [[item:Big Mushroom]] creates x2 Heal Powders. A [[item:Revival Herb]] creates x3 Heal Powders
Poultice: x1 [[item:Energy Powder]] and x1 [[item:Heal Powder]] create x3 [[item:Poultices]].

features.Name: Chemist
features.Effect: You may use any Chemistry Recipe for which you qualify using your [[item:Chemistry Set]].

features.Name: Chemical Warfare
features.Trigger: You throw a Pester Ball
features.Effect: The Pester Ball creates a Blast 2, affecting all targets in the area.

features.Name: Caustic Chemistry
features.Trigger: You hit with a Pester Ball or apply a Repel to a Pokémon
features.Effect: Make a Technology Education Roll. All targets affected by this Feature's trigger lose Hit Points equal to your roll. This may only affect a target once per Scene.

features.Name: Playing God
features.Effect:
Cost: ₽3500
Choose Castform, Grimer, Koffing, Magnemite, Porygon, Solosis, Trubbish, or Voltorb. Using your chemistry set, you create an artificial Egg of the Chosen Pokémon, that hatches within a day. The resulting Pokémon is born at level 5, with the Nature and Ability of your choice (Abilities chosen from its species' Basic Abilities). Additionally, you may enhance the Pokémon in several ways. Choose a number of upgrades below equal to your Technology Education Rank.
» The Pokémon is of an unusual coloration, gaining a +2d6 Bonus to the Introduction Stage of a Contest toward a single Contest Stat.
» The Pokémon adds a Move from its Egg Move or Move Tutor List to its Inheritance List. This may be performed up to 3 times.
» Increase one of the Pokémon's Base Stats by +1. This counts as use of a Vitamin. This may be performed up to 5 times.

recipes.Name: Enhancers
recipes.Effect: You can create any X-Item, [[item:Dire Hit]], or [[item:Guard Spec]].

recipes.Name: Pester Balls: Disorient
recipes.Effect: You create [[item:Pester Balls]] that can inflict [[status:Rage]] or [[status:Confusion]].

recipes.Name: Pester Balls: Pain
recipes.Effect: You create [[item:Pester Balls]] that can inflict Burn or Poison.

recipes.Name: Pester Balls: Shut Down
recipes.Effect: You create [[item:Pester Balls]] that can inflict [[status:Paralysis]] or [[status:Sleep]].

features.Name: Climatology
features.Effect: You gain the [[ability:Overcoat]] Ability.

features.Name: Weather Control
features.Trigger: A Move or Ability creates a Weather Effect while non-standard [[keyword:Weather]] is already in effect
features.Effect: The triggering Weather Effect does not replace the already extant [[keyword:Weather]] in effect; both exist simultaneously on the field. If a new [[keyword:Weather]] effect is placed on the field after the two that are out, both are replaced by the third, unless you activate this Feature again to replace only one.

features.Name: Weather Systems
features.Target: Your Pokémon with at least 2 Tutor Points
features.Effect: Your Pokémon loses 2 Tutor Points, and learns your choice of [[move:Hail]], [[move:Rain Dance]], [[move:Sandstorm]], or [[move:Sunny Day]]. The target must be able to learn the chosen Move through Level-Up, TM, or Tutor Moves. If the target has the chosen Move in their Level-Up List, [[feature:Weather Systems]] costs no Tutor Points.

features.Name: Extreme Weather
features.Trigger: You or your Pokémon create a Weather Condition
features.Effect:
The Weather is particularly intense and has additional effects.
» [[move:Hail]]: All Trainers and Pokémon that take Hail Damage take a -5 Penalty to all Damage Rolls.
» Rain: All Trainers and Pokémon that are not Water or Grass typed are [[status:Slowed]].
» [[move:Sandstorm]]: All Trainers and Pokémon that take [[move:Sandstorm]] damage take a -2 Penalty to Accuracy Rolls.
» Sun: Trainers and Pokémon that are not Fire or Grass Typed are [[status:Suppressed]].

features.Name: Witch Hunter
features.Prerequisites: Occultism Research Field, Novice Occult Education
features.Effect: You gain the [[feature:Psionic Sight]] Feature, even if you do not meet the prerequisites. If you already had the [[feature:Psionic Sight]] Feature, you instead gain another Feature for which you qualify.

features.Name: Psionic Analysis
features.Effect:
You are able to analyze Psychic Residue and can determine the following information about the Trainer or Pokémon that left the residue:
» Whether they are a Human or a Pokémon
» Which Psychic-Type Moves they know
» If they're Human, which of the following Class Features they have: [[feature:Telepath]], [[feature:Telekinetic]], [[feature:Warper]]

features.Name: Mental Resistance
features.Effect: You gain the [[capability:Mindlock]] Capability and 10 Damage Reduction against Special Psychic, Ghost, and Dark-Type damage.

features.Name: Immutable Mind
features.Trigger: You're hit by a Psychic, Ghost, or Dark-Type Move
features.Effect: If the triggering Move was a Status-Class Move, the Move fails. If the Triggering Move was a Damaging Move with a Secondary Effect that triggers on a certain roll, you are immune to the secondary effect.

features.Name: Fossil Restoration
features.Prerequisites: Paleontology Research Field, [[edge:Paleontologist]], Novice Pokémon Education
features.Target: A Fossil you are reviving
features.Effect: You may revive a Fossil into a Fossil Pokémon. The resulting Pokémon is born with 2 Tutor Points, and gains its first Basic Ability. If it has only one Basic Ability, it gains one of its Advanced Abilities, chosen by the GM. This Feature does not affect how the Pokémon continues to gain Abilities.

features.Name: Ancient Heritage
features.Target: Your Fossil Pokémon with at least 2 Tutor Points remaining
features.Effect: The target loses 2 Tutor Points and learns [[move:Ancient Power]]. If the target has [[move:Ancient Power]] in its Level-Up List, [[feature:Ancient Heritage]] costs no Tutor Points. As a static effect, whenever your Pokémon use [[move:Ancient Power]], its activated effect occurs on 18+ and you may always choose whether it deals Physical or Special Damage, using the appropriate attack Stat.

features.Name: Genetic Memory
features.Target: Your Fossil Pokémon with at least 2 Tutor Points remaining
features.Effect: The target loses 2 Tutor Points and learns any Move from its Egg Move or Tutor Move List. [[feature:Genetic Memory]] may target a Pokémon only twice: once with a Tutor Move and once with an Egg Move. Egg Moves tutored this way do not count against the limit of 3 for TM and Tutor Moves.

features.Name: Prehistoric Bond
features.Target: The remains of a Fossil you revived
features.Effect: You also produce a Held Item from the remnants of the Fossil. The effect of this Held Item is based on the highest Base Stat of the individual Pokémon being Revived, counting the effects of Nature but no other effects that alter Base Stats. If there is a tie, the GM decides which Base Stat is used. This Held Item may only be used by Pokémon revived from Fossils.

features.Name: Pusher
features.Prerequisites: Pokémon Caretaking Research Field, Novice Pokémon Education
features.Effect: Your Pokémon gain the [[pokeedge:Basic Ranged Attacks]], [[pokeedge:Aura Pulse]], [[pokeedge:Enticing Bait]], [[pokeedge:Extended Invisibility]], [[pokeedge:Far Reading]], [[pokeedge:Precise Threadings]], [[pokeedge:Seismometer]], [[pokeedge:TK Mastery]], and [[pokeedge:Trail Sniffer]] Poke Edges automatically if they qualify for them, without having to invest any Tutor Points.

features.Name: This One's Special, I Know It
features.Target: A hatching egg.
features.Effect: The Pokémon is born with special qualities, determined by the GM. This Feature may be activated one time per Pokémon Education Rank above Untrained.

features.Name: Skill Trainer
features.Trigger: You Train your Pokémon
features.Effect: For each of your Pokémon that has been Trained during this time, choose a Skill; that Skill becomes Pushed until an Extended Rest is taken. Pokémon rolls +1d6 with Pushed Skills, unless that would cause you to roll more than 6d6; if so, that Pokémon rolls with a +3 Bonus instead. A Pokémon may have only one Pushed Skill at a time.

features.Name: Re-Balancing
features.Target: A Pokémon with 2 Tutor Points
features.Effect: The target loses 2 Tutor Points, and gains one of the following: +1 to all Base Stats, +2 to two different Base Stats, or +3 to a single Base Stat. The target then redistributes their Stat Points. A Pokémon may be targeted by [[feature:Re-Balancing]] only once.

features.Name: Improvised Gadgets
features.Prerequisites: Gadgeteer Research Field, Novice Technology Education
features.Target: A willing Pokémon with the [[capability:Magnetic]], [[capability:Zapper]], or [[capability:Threaded]] Capability
features.Effect: Choose one of the Capabilities listed in the Target line that the target Pokémon has. You create a Main or Off-Hand Equipment Item usable by Trainers that grants the user the chosen Capability. Whenever a Trainer makes Struggle Attacks using [[capability:Zapper]] through this Item, they may choose to use your Technology Education Rank tripled in place of an offensive Stat. When this Feature is Unbound, the Equipment Item breaks and cannot be repaired. You may only have X instances of this Feature Bound at once, where X is equal to half your Technology Education Rank.

features.Name: I Meant to Do That
features.Trigger: You must have at least one Equipment Item you created with [[feature:Improvised Gadgets]] equipped to use this Feature.
features.Effect:
Choose one of your equipped items you created with Improved Gadgets. It is destroyed and cannot be repaired, and that instance of [[feature:Improvised Gadgets]] is immediately Unbound. Use the effect below corresponding to the Capability granted by the chosen item.
» [[capability:Magnetic]]: You may activate this effect as a Standard Action Interrupt whenever a Steel or Electric-Type attack or an attack with a metal Weapon would hit a target within 5 meters. The attack instead misses all targets within 5 meters.
» [[capability:Threaded]]: Choose up to 3 targets within 4 meters and perform an AC 4 Status Attack against them as a Standard Action. All hit targets become [[status:Stuck]] and [[status:Trapped]] for one full round.
[[capability:Zapper]]: You may activate this effect as a Swift Action upon hitting a foe with a [[capability:Zapper]]-modified Struggle Attack. The foe is Paralyzed.

features.Name: Capsule Science
features.Effect:
You learn the Cap Cannon, Cap Ammo, and [[item:Wonder Launcher]] recipes, and you gain the following additional effects when using those items.
» Bean Caps: You gain a +10 Damage Bonus when using Bean Caps.
» Glue Caps: Your Effect Range when using Glue Caps is increased by +3.
» Net Caps: Targets affected by your Net Caps gain a -X penalty to all Damage Rolls, where X is your Technology Education Rank.
» [[item:Wonder Launcher]]: Whenever you apply an item to a target using the [[item:Wonder Launcher]], they gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Technology Education Rank.

features.Name: Enhanced Capsules
features.Target: A willing Pokémon with one of the Capabilities listed below
features.Effect:
Choose one of the Capabilities below which the target Pokémon has. You create a consumable item with the effect below, depending on the chosen Capability. All unused items created with [[feature:Enhanced Capsules]] are rendered inert after an Extended Rest (including modifications to other items).
» [[capability:Glow]]: This item may be attached to a [[item:Wonder Launcher]] as a Standard Action to give the following effect for the rest of the Scene: Whenever you apply an Item to a target using this [[item:Wonder Launcher]], that target gains the [[ability:Illuminate]] Ability for one full round.
» [[capability:Magnetic]]: This item may be loaded into a Cap Cannon to provide two Bean Cap Ammo. When fired, these Bean Caps cannot miss.
» [[capability:Threaded]]: This item may be loaded into a Cap Cannon to provide two Glue Cap Ammo. When fired, they affect a Blast 2 instead of a single target.
» [[capability:Zapper]]: This item may be loaded into a Cap Cannon as a single Net Cap Ammo. Targets trapped by this Net Cap are [[status:Suppressed]] while trapped. Targets immune to Electric-Type attacks are immune to this effect.

features.Name: Engineer
features.Effect: You may craft any Engineer Recipe for which you qualify.

features.Name: Robofighter
features.Effect: As long as this Feature is Bound, you can command your Pokébot using a Standard Action rather than a Pokémon turn. Your Pokébots may still only act once a round.

features.Name: Overclock
features.Target: Your Pokébot
features.Effect: The target is cured of all Persistent Statuses, resets all negative Combat Stages to default, and gains two Ticks of Temporary Hit Points. For the rest of the Scene, it deals and takes additional damage with all attacks equal to your Technology Education Rank.

features.Name: Experimental AI
features.Effect: Increase the maximum complexity of all Pokébots you create by 2, and increase the maximum complexity of Pokébots you can control by 2.

recipes.Name: Robotics 101
recipes.Effect: You can create a Small Pokébot for ₽1000, a Medium Pokébot for ₽2000, or a Large Pokébot for ₽3000. Pokébots you create begin at Level 5. You can create and install Basic Combat and Basic Utility Parts for Pokébots.

recipes.Name: Firmware Update
recipes.Effect: You can create and install Advanced Combat and Advanced Utility Parts for Pokébots.

recipes.Name: Kitbash King
recipes.Effect: You can create and install Sympathetic Drives and Repair Nanites for Pokébots.

recipes.Name: Futuretech
recipes.Effect: You can create and install Wired Compatibility Cores for Pokébots.

features.Name: Jailbreaker
features.Effect: You may craft any Poké Ball Case Recipe for which you qualify.

features.Name: Poké Ball Mods
features.Effect: You may craft any of the Poké Ball Modifications on the next page.

features.Name: Fusion Cases
features.Effect: You combine two different [[item:Poké Ball Cases]] into a single Fusion Case with both effects and types. [[feature:Fusion Cases]] may not be used as Ingredients for this Feature.

features.Name: Case Specialist
features.Trigger: You hit a target with a Poké Ball with a Spray, [[move:Flash]], [[move:Bounce]], or [[item:Zap Case]] applied to it.
features.Effect:
The Case has additional effects according to its type(s).
» [[item:Spray Case]]: After resolving the effects of the Case, the target loses a Tick of Health Points for each Persistent or Volatile Status Affliction they have. This may only affect a target once per Scene.
» [[item:Flash Case]]: The Case uses the Move [[move:Flash]] as a Burst 2 instead of a Cone 2
» [[item:Bounce Case]]: The Poké Ball bounces an additional time. This may not cause it to hit a target more than once.
» [[item:Zap Case]]: The target can only use At-Will actions until the end of their next turn. This may only affect a target once per Scene.

recipes.Name: Basic Cases
recipes.Effect: You may create a [[item:Contest Case]], [[item:Lock Case]], or [[item:Medicine Case]] for ₽200.

recipes.Name: Trick Cases
recipes.Effect: You may create a [[item:Spray Case]], [[item:Flash Case]], or [[item:Bounce Case]] for ₽400.

recipes.Name: Advanced Cases
recipes.Effect: You may create a [[item:Zap Case]] for ₽500, a [[item:Devil Case]] for ₽1000, or a [[item:Storage Case]] for ₽5000.

features.Name: Upgrader
features.Prerequisites: [[feature:Upgrader]] Research Field, Novice Medicine Edu, Novice Technology Edu
features.Effect: You may craft any Augmentation Recipe for which you qualify and install them on yourself and willing Pokémon and Trainers.

features.Name: Emergency Reactivation
features.Trigger: You or your Pokémon suffer Augmentation Shock
features.Effect: The triggering user does not suffer Augmentation Shock and their Augmentations are not disabled. This Feature may affect a target only once per Scene.

features.Name: Efficient Installation
features.Effect: You and your Pokémon gain a +2 boost to their maximum Augmentation Capacity and count their used Capacity as 2 lower for the purposes of Augmentation Shock. You and your Pokémon can install multiple Augmentations in the same Slot.

features.Name: Experimental Designs
features.Target: You or your Pokémon with Augmentations
features.Effect:
Choose an Augmentation the target has and apply the upgrade below. [[feature:Experimental Designs]] may affect a target twice.
» Enhanced Sight: The user gains the [[capability:X-Ray Vision]] Capability.
» Smart Vision: The user learns the Move [[move:Feint]] without taking a Move Slot.
» Synthetic Muscle: The user recovers from Injuries twice as fast and heals one more Injury per day.
» Embedded Weaponry: The weapon is Fine and gains Deadly Strike as a Master Move.
» Wired Reflexes: The user gains one more Reflex Point per Scene and may also spend Reflex Points to gain +2 Critical Hit Range for one full round.
» Medical Nanobots: Once a Scene, the user may cure themselves of all Persistent Status Afflictions as a Standard Action.
» Dermal Plating: The user may also activate Dermal Plating to resist Special Damage.
» Thermal-Optic Camo: While active, the user is invisible to Aura Reading and [[feature:Thought Detection]].

recipes.Name: Datajack
recipes.Effect: You may build and install the Datajack Augmentaion for ₽250.

recipes.Name: Eye Augments
recipes.Effect: You may build and install the Enhanced Sight Augmentation for ₽1000 and Smart Vision Augmentation for ₽1500.

recipes.Name: Limb Augments
recipes.Effect: You build and install the Synthetic Muscle Augmentation for ₽1000 and the Embedded Weaponry Augmentation for ₽2000.

recipes.Name: Body Augments
recipes.Effect: You may build and install the Medical Nanobots Augmentation for ₽1000 and the Wired Reflexes Augmentation for ₽1500.

recipes.Name: Dermal Augments
recipes.Effect: You may build and install the Dermal Plating Augmentation for ₽2000 and the Thermal-Optic Camo Augmentation for ₽4000.

features.Name: Survivalist
features.Effect: Choose a Terrain in which you have spent at least three nights. You gain [[capability:Naturewalk]] for that terrain and a +2 bonus to Athletics, Acrobatics, Stealth, Perception, and Survival Checks in that terrain. When you have 2 [[feature:Survivalist]] Features, you may choose a second Terrain. When you have 4 [[feature:Survivalist]] Features, you may choose a third terrain. When you have 6 [[feature:Survivalist]] Features, you may choose a fourth terrain.

features.Name: Natural Fighter
features.Effect:
You and your Pokémon become adept at using the environment to your advantage in battle. You or your Pokémon may activate [[feature:Natural Fighter]] as a Standard Action to use the Move below corresponding to the current terrain. You and your Pokémon must still follow all Frequency limitations for the Move.
Grassland: [[move:Cotton Spore]]; Forest: [[move:Grass Whistle]]; Wetlands: [[move:Mud-Slap]]; Ocean: [[move:Aqua Ring]]; Tundra: [[move:Haze]]; Mountain: [[move:Smack Down]]; Cave: [[move:Astonish]]; Urban: [[move:Spikes]]; Desert: [[move:Sand Attack]]
features.Note: GMs! Don't be super duper strict about the terrains here. Obviously a beach is analogous enough to a desert to use [[move:Sand Attack]], and a lake can count as ocean terrain. In urban terrain, there'll probably at least be trash around to [[move:Fling]] with the standard 6 DB option. On the other hand, most standard arenas for League matches won't qualify for any of the terrains. However, some arenas may be specifically designed to emulate a terrain type, such as a rocky stadium or a set of floating platforms in a pool.

features.Name: Trapper
features.Effect:
You create a consumable item that creates 8 meters of [[keyword:Hazard]] within 6 meters. All 8 meters must be adjacent with at least one other space of the [[keyword:Hazard]]. These Hazards cause foes that run into them to become [[status:Slowed]] until the end of their next turn and have an additional effect based on the terrain in which the item was made. When foes run into these Hazards, they are destroyed after their effects resolve. Pokémon and Trainers with [[capability:Naturewalk]] for the terrains associated with a [[keyword:Hazard]] are immune to its effects. These items must be used the same day they are created or they lose all effect.
» Dust Trap — Grassland or Desert: A foe that runs into this [[keyword:Hazard]] is Blinded until the end of their next turn.
» Tangle Trap — Forest or Wetlands: A foe that runs into this [[keyword:Hazard]] is must immediately stop Shifting, and they are [[status:Stuck]] instead of [[status:Slowed]] until the end of their next turn.
» Slick Trap — Ocean or Tundra: A foe that runs into this [[keyword:Hazard]] becomes [[status:Vulnerable]] until the end of their next Turn.
» Abrasion Trap — Mountain, Cave, or Urban: A foe that runs into this [[keyword:Hazard]] lowers their Defense and Special Defense by 1 Combat Stage.

features.Name: Wilderness Guide
features.Effect:
[[feature:Wilderness Guide]]'s effect depends on your current terrain.
» Grassland or Forest: All allies gain the Stealth Capability and a +2 bonus to their Overland Speed for one full round.
» Ocean or Wetlands: All allies gain 5 Damage Reduction and a +2 bonus to their Swim Speed for one full round.
» Desert or Tundra: All allies do not lose Hit Points from [[keyword:Weather]] and ignore the effects of foes' [[ability:Sand Veil]] and [[ability:Snow Cloak]] Abilities for one full round.
» Mountain or Cave: All allies do not trigger Hazards and are not Blinded in Low-Light conditions for one full round.
» Urban: All allies gain +1 Evasion and a +2 bonus on Accuracy Rolls and Skill Checks to perform the Dirty Trick and Manipulate Combat Maneuvers for one full round.

features.Name: Terrain Talent
features.Effect: Each Rank, you gain two [[feature:Terrain Talents]], chosen from the Terrains for which you gained [[capability:Naturewalk]] from [[feature:Survivalist]].
features.Note: You do not have to be in the corresponding terrain to take advantage of [[feature:Terrain Talents]]! They work everywhere.

features.Name: Adaptive Geography
features.Trigger: You or your Pokémon gain Initiative
features.Effect: The triggering target takes their turn as if they were in a terrain adjacent to the terrain they are in on the following graphic. For example, if you are standing in Wetlands terrain, you may act as if you are standing in Forest or Ocean Terrain. This affects [[feature:Survivalist]] Features, [[capability:Naturewalk]] Capabilities Moves with the [[keyword:Environ]] Keyword, etc.

talents.Name: Plains Runner – Grassland Terrain
talents.Effect: Your Overland Speed is increased by +2. You gain a +2 bonus to Perception Checks to spot or identify objects in the far distance.

talents.Name: Forest Ranger – Forest Terrain
talents.Effect: You're used to navigating the dense plant life of large forests. You gain the Stealth Capability.

talents.Name: Marsh Stomper – Wetland Terrain
talents.Effect: You can handle the toxic fauna and flora of the marshes. You do not lose Hit Points from Poison and lose only 1 instead of 2 Combat Stages from Poison. You still count as [[status:Poisoned]] for the purpose of Moves and effects.

talents.Name: Deep Diver – Ocean Terrain
talents.Effect: You love nothing better than the smell of the sea. Your Swimming Capability is equal to your Overland Capability instead of half. Additionally, you may hold your breath underwater for a number of minutes equal to your Survival Rank before you start suffocating.

talents.Name: Arctic Pilgrim – Tundra Terrain
talents.Effect: Neither deep slow nor slippery ice can deter you. You are immune to the effects of [[move:Hail]] and to the [[status:Frozen]] condition, and gain 5 Damage Reduction against Ice-Type attacks.

talents.Name: Surefooted – Mountain Terrain
talents.Effect: You're not afraid of precarious ledges and steep hills. You gain a +2 Bonus to Skill Checks made to climb, balance, or maintain footing – including resisting [[keyword:Push]] and Trip maneuvers. Whenever you take falling damage, ignore one meter and receive one less Injury when determining damage.

talents.Name: Cave Dweller – Cave Terrain
talents.Effect: Your eyes are used to very low levels of light. You do not suffer [[status:Blindness]] for being in Low-Light conditions. If you would be Totally Blinded by complete darkness, you instead suffer the penalties of [[status:Blindness]], and may make Survival Checks instead of Acrobatics to avoid becoming [[status:Tripped]]. You are immune to [[move:Stealth Rock]] Hazards.

talents.Name: Traceur – Urban Terrain
talents.Effect: The city is your jungle. You gain a +1 Bonus to your Jump Capabilities. Add half your Survival Rank to your Evasion against [[keyword:Push]], Trip, and Attack of Opportunity Maneuvers.

talents.Name: Dune Walker – Desert Terrain
talents.Effect: Your long hours in the unforgiving desert have made you inured to sand and heat. You're immune to the effects of [[move:Sandstorm]], Sand-Attack, and [[move:Sand Tomb]], and you gain 5 Damage Reduction against Fire-Type attacks.

features.Name: Survivalist
features.Effect: Choose a Terrain in which you have spent at least three nights. You gain [[capability:Naturewalk]] for that terrain and a +2 bonus to Athletics, Acrobatics, Stealth, Perception, and Survival Checks in that terrain. When you have 2 [[feature:Survivalist]] Features, you may choose a second Terrain. When you have 4 [[feature:Survivalist]] Features, you may choose a third terrain. When you have 6 [[feature:Survivalist]] Features, you may choose a fourth terrain.

features.Name: Natural Fighter
features.Effect:
You and your Pokémon become adept at using the environment to your advantage in battle. You or your Pokémon may activate [[feature:Natural Fighter]] as a Standard Action to use the Move below corresponding to the current terrain. You and your Pokémon must still follow all Frequency limitations for the Move.
Grassland: [[move:Cotton Spore]]; Forest: [[move:Grass Whistle]]; Wetlands: [[move:Mud-Slap]]; Ocean: [[move:Aqua Ring]]; Tundra: [[move:Haze]]; Mountain: [[move:Smack Down]]; Cave: [[move:Astonish]]; Urban: [[move:Fling]]; Desert: [[move:Sand Attack]]
features.Note: GMs! Don't be super duper strict about the terrains here. Obviously a beach is analogous enough to a desert to use [[move:Sand Attack]], and a lake can count as ocean terrain. In urban terrain, there'll probably at least be trash around to [[move:Fling]] with the standard 6 DB option. On the other hand, most standard arenas for League matches won't qualify for any of the terrains. However, some arenas may be specifically designed to emulate a terrain type, such as a rocky stadium or a set of floating platforms in a pool.

features.Name: Trapper
features.Effect:
You create a consumable item that creates 8 meters of [[keyword:Hazard]] within 6 meters. All 8 meters must be adjacent with at least one other space of the [[keyword:Hazard]]. These Hazards cause foes that run into them to become [[status:Slowed]] until the end of their next turn and have an additional effect based on the terrain in which the item was made. When foes run into these Hazards, they are destroyed after their effects resolve. Pokémon and Trainers with [[capability:Naturewalk]] for the terrains associated with a [[keyword:Hazard]] are immune to its effects. These items must be used the same day they are created or they lose all effect.
» Dust Trap — Grassland or Desert: A foe that runs into this [[keyword:Hazard]] is Blinded until the end of their next turn.
» Tangle Trap — Forest or Wetlands: A foe that runs into this [[keyword:Hazard]] is must immediately stop Shifting, and they are [[status:Stuck]] instead of [[status:Slowed]] until the end of their next turn.
» Slick Trap — Ocean or Tundra: A foe that runs into this [[keyword:Hazard]] becomes [[status:Vulnerable]] until the end of their next Turn.
» Abrasion Trap — Mountain, Cave, or Urban: A foe that runs into this [[keyword:Hazard]] lowers their Defense and Special Defense by 1 Combat Stage.

features.Name: Wilderness Guide
features.Effect:
[[feature:Wilderness Guide]]'s effect depends on your current terrain.
» Grassland or Forest: All allies gain the Stealth Capability and a +2 bonus to their Overland Speed for one full round.
» Ocean or Wetlands: All allies gain 5 Damage Reduction and a +2 bonus to their Swim Speed for one full round.
» Desert or Tundra: All allies do not lose Hit Points from [[keyword:Weather]] and ignore the effects of foes' [[ability:Sand Veil]] and [[ability:Snow Cloak]] Abilities for one full round.
» Mountain or Cave: All allies do not trigger Hazards and are not Blinded in Low-Light conditions for one full round.
» Urban: All allies gain +1 Evasion and a +2 bonus on Accuracy Rolls and Skill Checks to perform the Dirty Trick and Manipulate Combat Maneuvers for one full round.

features.Name: Terrain Talent
features.Effect: Each Rank, you gain two [[feature:Terrain Talents]], chosen from the Terrains for which you gained [[capability:Naturewalk]] from [[feature:Survivalist]].
features.Note: You do not have to be in the corresponding terrain to take advantage of [[feature:Terrain Talents]]! They work everywhere.

features.Name: Adaptive Geography
features.Trigger: You or your Pokémon gain Initiative
features.Effect: The triggering target takes their turn as if they were in a terrain adjacent to the terrain they are in on the following graphic. For example, if you are standing in Wetlands terrain, you may act as if you are standing in Forest or Ocean Terrain. This affects [[feature:Survivalist]] Features, [[capability:Naturewalk]] Capabilities Moves with the [[keyword:Environ]] Keyword, etc.

talents.Name: Plains Runner – Grassland Terrain
talents.Effect: Your Overland Speed is increased by +2. You gain a +2 bonus to Perception Checks to spot or identify objects in the far distance.

talents.Name: Forest Ranger – Forest Terrain
talents.Effect: You're used to navigating the dense plant life of large forests. You gain the Stealth Capability.

talents.Name: Marsh Stomper – Wetland Terrain
talents.Effect: You can handle the toxic fauna and flora of the marshes. You do not lose Hit Points from Poison and lose only 1 instead of 2 Combat Stages from Poison. You still count as [[status:Poisoned]] for the purpose of Moves and effects.

talents.Name: Deep Diver – Ocean Terrain
talents.Effect: You love nothing better than the smell of the sea. Your Swimming Capability is equal to your Overland Capability instead of half. Additionally, you may hold your breath underwater for a number of minutes equal to your Survival Rank before you start suffocating.

talents.Name: Arctic Pilgrim – Tundra Terrain
talents.Effect: Neither deep slow nor slippery ice can deter you. You are immune to the effects of [[move:Hail]] and to the [[status:Frozen]] condition, and gain 5 Damage Reduction against Ice-Type attacks.

talents.Name: Surefooted – Mountain Terrain
talents.Effect: You're not afraid of precarious ledges and steep hills. You gain a +2 Bonus to Skill Checks made to climb, balance, or maintain footing – including resisting [[keyword:Push]] and Trip maneuvers. Whenever you take falling damage, ignore one meter and receive one less Injury when determining damage.

talents.Name: Cave Dweller – Cave Terrain
talents.Effect: Your eyes are used to very low levels of light. You do not suffer [[status:Blindness]] for being in Low-Light conditions. If you would be Totally Blinded by complete darkness, you instead suffer the penalties of [[status:Blindness]], and may make Survival Checks instead of Acrobatics to avoid becoming [[status:Tripped]]. You are immune to [[move:Stealth Rock]] Hazards.

talents.Name: Traceur – Urban Terrain
talents.Effect: The city is your jungle. You gain a +1 Bonus to your Jump Capabilities. Add half your Survival Rank to your Evasion against [[keyword:Push]], Trip, and Attack of Opportunity Maneuvers.

talents.Name: Dune Walker – Desert Terrain
talents.Effect: Your long hours in the unforgiving desert have made you inured to sand and heat. You're immune to the effects of [[move:Sandstorm]], Sand-Attack, and [[move:Sand Tomb]], and you gain 5 Damage Reduction against Fire-Type attacks.

features.Name: Athlete
features.Prerequisites: Novice Athletics, One of [[edge:Athletic Initiative]], [[edge:Mounted Prowess]], [[edge:Power Boost]], [[edge:Stamina]], or [[edge:Swimmer]]
features.Effect: After an hour of exercise, an [[feature:Athlete]] may choose two different Stats besides HP; both of those stats become Trained Stats. The default State of Trained Stats is +1 Combat Stages instead of 0. An Athlete may have two Trained Stats at a time.

features.Name: Training Regime
features.Effect:
You gain additional static bonuses based on your Trained Stats.
» Attack: You gain a +2 Bonus on Accuracy Checks to hit with Combat Maneuvers.
» Defense: You gain 5 Damage Reduction when Intercepting attacks.
» Special Attack: You may add half your Special Attack Stat to Damaging Athlete Moves. This does not stack with [[ability:Twisted Power]].
» Special Defense: You gain a +2 Bonus to Opposed Checks to resist Combat Maneuvers.
» Speed: When you [[ability:Sprint]], you double your Movement Capability instead of increasing by 50%.

features.Name: Coaching
features.Trigger: Your Pokémon makes a Combat Maneuver
features.Effect:
Your Pokémon gains a bonus based on the type of Combat maneuver they are making. This Feature may be triggered once per Scene per Pokémon.
» Your Pokémon gains a +1d6 bonus to Opposed Acrobatics, Athletics, Combat, or Stealth Skill Checks. » If your Pokémon was Sprinting, they double their Movement Capabilities instead of increasing by 50%.
» If your Pokémon was making an Attack of Opportunity, they automatically hit.
» You may also activate this Feature to let them Intercept for any Ally regardless of Loyalty, and they automatically succeed on the Skill Check to do so.

features.Name: Adrenaline Rush
features.Trigger: You are lowered to half or your Maximum Hit Points or less
features.Effect: You gain +1 Combat Stage in each of your Trained Stats, are cured of up to two Status Afflictions, and gain a Tick of Temporary Hit Points. [[feature:Adrenaline Rush]] may be used only once per Scene.

features.Name: Athletic Moves

features.Name: Dancer
features.Prerequisites: Novice Acrobatics; Novice Athletics or Novice Charm
features.Effect: Choose [[ability:Spinning Dance]] or [[ability:Own Tempo]]. You gain the chosen Ability.
features.Mechanic – Dance Moves: Dance Moves you create with the [[feature:Dance Form]] Feature look like the Move on the right. First, name the [[feature:Dance Move]] whatever you like. Secondly, choose two Combat Stage gains for the effect. This may either be +2 Combat Stages to a single Stat, like [[move:Swords Dance]], or +1 Combat Stage to two different Stats, like [[move:Dragon Dance]]. Once chosen, this cannot be changed. [[move:Dragon Dance]], [[move:Quiver Dance]], and [[move:Swords Dance]] count as Dance Moves for the purposes of [[feature:Dancer]] Features as well. A [[feature:Dance Move]]'s Contest Type must be chosen from a Contest Type associated with a Stat that the [[feature:Dance Move]] affects. Cool is associated with Attack, Tough is associated with Defense, Beauty is associated with Special Attack, Smart is associated with Special Defense, and Cute is associated with Speed.

features.Name: Beguiling Dance
